chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Ja'far ibn Bashir from Hammad ibn 'Uthman from Idris ibn 'Abdullah al-Qummi who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the man who is praying and parallel to him is a woman standing upon her bed by his side. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'If she was seated, it would not harm him, and if she was praying, then no (it does not harm him).'
ai.seo_question: Does a woman standing or sitting parallel to a man invalidate his prayer?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the fiqh of *sadd al-dhari’ah* (blocking the path of distraction) by distinguishing between a woman standing and one seated parallel to the praying man. While standing posture is more likely to cause visual distraction (*ghurur*) and thus invalidate the prayer, a seated position is deemed harmless, reflecting the Shia scholarly emphasis on practical ease and the specific nature of visual barriers in domestic settings.
